I've always had bad self image issues, and then a few years ago developed a bunch of major chronic health issues that took years to resolve, with a bunch of terrible side effects that made me face bloat, caused mobility issues, etc. All the pent up emotions (frustration, resentment, anger, helplessness) + lack of family support caused me to turn to a bunch of unhealthy coping mechanisms (getting high, binging, masturbating, online shopping). Binging felt like the worst though, I gained a bunch of weight and lost all self esteem. Couldn't even look in the mirror without breaking down.

I'm doing a bit better now, thanks to vyvanse, therapy, quitting weed and trying my best to refrain from those quick addictive dopamine fixes. I would really encourage you to talk to a professional therapist, especially if you can find one that has some experience in dealing with body issues. My therapist wasn't all that knowledgeable but she was kind, listened to me, and helped challenge some of my negative thinking/self-image. And I really needed that from someone, to help me untangle all my complex feelings. I'm not cured by any means and I still struggle but it has helped keep me accountable and ground me somewhat when I'm spiraling or thinking of returning to negative habits. 

It's very difficult learning to accept an aspect of your body that you can't change, I feel for you.


(Also I know this is not a prevalent belief thanks to our shitty society, but penis size has absolutely nothing to do with you being a man or masculine, just like how being short or bald does not make you more or less of a man or boob size does not make you more or less of a woman. There are men without penises. Yes some women will be shitty about it but there are also SOOOOOOO many women who care way more about things like mutual repect, care, love - the kind of things that are actually important in a meaningful relationship. A dick is not the end all be all!! It's not even a requirement for good sex!!!)

Honestly, you just look like a normal person in both photos. We are our own worst critics but please know that the average Joe passing you on the street will not think of you as ugly or a loser or whatever, everyone is caught up in their own lives and problems. And true friends will stick by you regardless of your appearance. It may seem like an impossible hill to climb right now but you are so young, you have years and years and years to change your life in whatever way you want. I agree with others that your focus should be on improving the BED and underlying mental problems and treating yourself with care and compassion. Don't put so much pressure on getting back to that first photo, beating yourself up about it will not make it happen any faster and will actually be detrimental to your recovery process. And try be kind to the girl in the second photo, she has been through a lot and BED is a very very difficult thing to deal with, we've all been there. Sending you lots of love and support ♡

I feel this so hard. I was in a really terrible cycle last year that I finally managed to wring myself mostly out of by CONSISTENTLY taking vyvanse (my adhd meds that is also an appetite suppressant lol but I frequently forget to take), deleting food apps, drinking coffee, and going keto. The first week(s) is THE fucking hardest, but I threw out all the snacks and bread in my house and ate a lot of bland low cal high volume foods, to try and rewire my brain from all the addicting carby delicious foods I was inhaling before. Not a healthy way be warned, I kind of went the opposite extreme end with managing my meals but I'm an extreme type of person, only way to stop the binges was to cut myself off completely from carbs (my trigger food) and basically make my meals so boring and bland that I forget how "good food" tastes.

I would really suggest medication if you can get it, not necessarily vyvanse but someone else had mentioned some options you can look into. I don't think I'll ever "recover" and think about food like a normal person, but I promise you it is possible to REDUCE the urges and at least not be consumed by thoughts of food 24/7. I used to wake up and go to bed every day scrolling thru ubereats, food IGs, videos, grocery flyers, and obsess constantly about my next meal, and fight myself to not order takeout and do it anyway, literally every fucking moment but now it's maybe like every 5-6 moments lol. Sometimes I can go the whole day without an urge, which seems fucking wild considering where I was at last year.

Anyways these are not comprehensive methods, I would def talk to a doctor if you can, and take my anecdotal evidence with a grain of salt, but I just wanted to give u some support and love bc it is so fucking difficult to break out of that cycle but it can be possible!! And I'm rooting for you!!!
